To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have detected the radio counterparts to 10 out of 11 SMGs, (2) we have found that the submillimeter emission of SMGs is typically extended on scales of 1-3 kpc, and (3), we have found evidence for a population peaking at high redshifts of extremely luminous SMGs with low radio fluxes.
we have found evidence of a population of extremely dusty, extremely luminous, and radio-weak high-redshift SMGs that may have important consequences for galaxy formation and dust production models.
we have confirmed the radio-submillmeter association, and we have discovered that a significant population of radio-dim, high-redshift sub-mm galaxies exists.

understanding the formation and evolution of massive star-forming galaxies at high redshift.
the nature and origin of the most massive galaxies in the Universe, as well as the physical conditions and properties of the dust in these objects.
the physical nature of high-redshift SMGs, which are the most luminous, star-forming galaxies in the early Universe.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SMG population is more diverse than we previously thought.
the SMGs are not a monolithic population, and that the radio and submillimeter are not necessarily good tracers of each other.

the submillimeter selection is an excellent way to find the highest luminosity, most massive, star-forming galaxies at z > 2, and the radio selection is an excellent complement to this, allowing us to probe the nature of the star-forming galaxies in more detail.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the submillimeter-selected SMG population is not simply an extension of the radio-selected population to higher redshift.
the radio-submillmeter association is not complete, and the population of radio-faint SMGs is a significant component of the SMG population.
, while the radio and submillimeter morphologies of SMGs appear similar, the radio emission is not a complete tracer of the submillimeter emission.
